title: Reverse Centaurs, AI, and the Classroom
author: Peter Greene
summary: Cory Doctorow's concept of reverse centaurs illuminates the real danger of AI in education: not replacement, but degradation of human labor into subordinate support for machines. Greene explains that a centaur is a human enhanced by machines, while a reverse centaur is a human serving as a squishy appendage for an uncaring machine. In schools, this manifests as teachers checking AI-generated work to catch rare errors, or guides monitoring AI instruction in stripped-down charter schools. The article argues through detailed examples that AI companies market AI as both a productivity tool to management and an empowering centaur to teachers, when the reality is likely reverse centaur status for both. The rhetorical move is to shift the conversation away from AI capability and toward labor dynamics and power relationships in education.
points: The key question is not whether AI can do a teacher's job, but whether the human in the loop serves the AI or is served by it.
Charter and online schools use low-wage guides as accountability sinks to absorb blame for AI mistakes.
Teachers must ask whether proposed AI tools will empower them (centaur) or convert them to support structures (reverse centaur).
The promise that AI will increase efficiency appeals to managers precisely because efficiency in personnel-heavy fields means fewer people.
AI cannot do a teacher's job, which is why there will always be a human in the loop, but that human's role is being defined downward.
